strengths: Proposes a diffusion-based warping-and-inpainting framework for joint novel-view image and geometry synthesis from unposed sparse reference images, supporting extrapolative and zero-shot settings.
Introduces cross-modal attention instillation to inject image-branch spatial attention into the geometry branch, improving cross-modal alignment between generated images and geometry.
Proximity-based mesh conditioning integrates depth/normal cues and normal masking to handle noisy and erroneous projected point clouds.
Reports strong quantitative results on DTU and RealEstate10K, with competitive or state-of-the-art performance in extrapolative and interpolative NVS settings.
Demonstrates qualitative multi-view generalization and can accept arbitrary numbers of reference views at inference despite two-view training.
Provides ablations for key components and shows progressive performance improvements.
weaknesses: Appendix Table 5 is explicitly marked 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled,' which seriously undermines completeness, reproducibility, and confidence in the geometry evaluation.

Both training supervision and geometry evaluation rely on pseudo ground-truth geometry predicted by VGGT, the same family of off-the-shelf geometry models used for conditioning, creating potential circularity and limiting claims of true geometric accuracy.

Missing quantitative comparisons against several leading generative/feedforward NVS methods such as LVSM, CAT3D, and ReconFusion; LVSM is only compared qualitatively, weakening state-of-the-art claims.

The cross-modal attention instillation is applied only from the image branch to the geometry branch, yet the claimed regularization of image generation by geometry is not clearly formalized or separately ablated.
Ablation does not isolate the individual contributions of proximity-based mesh conditioning (mesh conversion, depth/normal concatenation, normal masking).
Training details for the two-stage fine-tuning procedure, loss weighting, and exact cross-modal attention schedule are insufficient for full reproducibility.
Evaluation on Co3D is mostly qualitative; no quantitative comparison on this dataset is provided.
Minor clarity issues include inconsistent terminology ('distillation' vs. 'instillation'), typographical errors, and some dataset citation/caption errors.
Broader ethical implications of high-fidelity novel-view synthesis are not discussed.

strengths: Addresses a challenging and relevant problem: joint novel-view image and geometry synthesis from unposed sparse reference views, including extrapolative settings.
The warping-and-inpainting formulation is extended from single-image to multi-view and to explicit geometry completion without per-scene optimization, which is a sensible direction.
Cross-modal attention instillation is an interesting mechanism: using image U-Net queries/keys to drive geometry U-Net attention could encourage semantic alignment between modalities.
Proximity-based mesh conditioning with depth/normal cues and normal masking is a practical strategy for handling noisy, sparse projected point clouds.
The method supports pose-free inputs and variable numbers of reference views at inference, which improves flexibility over many pose-embedded generative NVS models.

Quantitative image results on DTU and RealEstate10K show improvements over several baselines in extrapolative settings, and qualitative results demonstrate plausible scene completion and aligned colored point clouds.
The ablation study shows progressive gains from pointmap conditioning, mesh conditioning, and cross-modal attention, even if the individual improvements are modest.
The paper is generally readable, with a reasonably clear motivation and related-work section.
weaknesses: The geometry supervision and evaluation are fundamentally problematic: the geometry branch is trained against pseudo ground-truth pointmaps produced by VGGT, and the reported geometry metrics appear to compare against VGGT-derived geometry rather than true 3D ground truth. This makes the central geometry-quality claims circular and largely measures agreement with VGGT, not genuine novel-view geometry accuracy.

There are no external baselines for the geometry completion task, and the image tables do not report true depth/geometry errors. The paper claims well-aligned geometry synthesis but provides no quantitative alignment metric between generated images and generated geometry.

The formal definition of extrapolative viewpoints is mathematically flawed: camera poses in SE(3) do not form a vector space, so a convex combination of poses, π_t = Σ α_n π_n, is not well-defined. This weakens the experimental protocol and the claimed extrapolative evaluation.

Several evaluation results are counterintuitive or inconsistent. In some tables, extrapolative PSNR is higher than interpolative PSNR for the same method, which is suspicious and suggests that the extrapolative/interpolative splits or target selection may be unreliable.

The DTU table caption/reference is incorrect (DTU is cited as [34], which is RealEstate10K), and the target-view/pose setup for pose-free baselines is not fully explained, raising concerns about fair comparison.

Cross-modal attention instillation is insufficiently specified for reproducibility. The paper does not clearly describe layer-wise injection, resolution mismatches, which attention layers are replaced, how gradients from the geometry branch affect the image branch, or how training proceeds before/after attention sharing.

An important component, camera-space pointmap normalization, is introduced only in the appendix, despite the appendix claiming it is critical for performance. This omission from the main method hurts clarity and reproducibility.

Proximity-based mesh conditioning lacks sensitivity analysis and component ablations: ball-pivoting parameters, normal-masking thresholds, and the separate effect of depth/normal conditioning are not evaluated.

The novelty is incremental: the work combines warping-and-inpainting, off-the-shelf geometry prediction, diffusion inpainting, and cross-modal attention. The attention-instillation mechanism is not analyzed deeply enough to establish it as a substantial conceptual advance over attention distillation or cross-modal feature injection.

Comparisons to relevant generative NVS methods such as Zero-1-to-3, CAT3D, or MVDream are mostly discussed but not quantitatively evaluated, despite the paper positioning itself against pose-embedded generative models.
The LVSM comparison is only qualitative, and no quantitative comparison is given, even though LVSM is described as a leading feedforward NVS approach.

The reported ablation gains are modest: cross-modal attention improves PSNR by about 0.4 over mesh conditioning, and mesh conditioning by only about 0.08 over pointmap conditioning. This weakens the claim that each component is decisively responsible for the final performance.

The claim of state-of-the-art extrapolative performance is stronger than the evidence supports, given the limited and partly circular geometry evaluation, missing geometry baselines, and inconsistent camera-split protocol.

strengths: Proposes a unified diffusion framework that jointly synthesizes novel-view images and aligned geometry from unposed sparse reference views, targeting extrapolative NVS and 3D completion.
Introduces cross-modal attention instillation (MoAI), a simple but effective mechanism that couples image and geometry diffusion branches; ablations show consistent gains in PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS.
Proximity-based mesh conditioning mitigates noisy sparse point-cloud projections via mesh interpolation, depth/normal cues, and normal masking; ablation supports its contribution.
Strong empirical results on DTU zero-shot and RealEstate10K, especially in extrapolative settings, with large improvements over PixelSplat, MVSplat, NoPoSplat, LucidDreamer, and GenWarp.
Generalizes to an arbitrary number of reference views at inference despite fixed-view training, demonstrating flexible multi-view aggregated attention.
Qualitative results show plausible extrapolation and aligned geometry, producing colored point clouds for 3D scene completion without per-scene NeRF/3DGS optimization.
weaknesses: The submitted manuscript contains an incomplete appendix table (Table 5: 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled'), which is unacceptable for review and undermines completeness and reproducibility.

Geometry supervision and evaluation rely heavily on VGGT pseudo-ground-truth pointmaps. If geometry metrics are also computed against VGGT predictions, the evaluation is circular and does not establish true novel-view geometry accuracy against real 3D ground truth.

Missing quantitative comparisons against recent generative NVS methods such as CAT3D, ReconFusion, SV3D, and Gen3C; LVSM is only compared qualitatively. Most baselines are non-generative feedforward or warping methods, so the generative NVS positioning is not fully supported.

Terminology is inconsistent: the abstract says 'cross-modal attention distillation' while the method uses attention sharing/instillation without a distillation loss. The theoretical justification for replacing geometry attention maps is limited.
Proximity-based mesh conditioning lacks implementation details, including ball-pivoting parameters, normal-threshold sensitivity, and failure cases, making reproducibility harder.

Some claims are overstated: e.g., 'state-of-the-art ... interpolative' is not fully supported because NoPoSplat achieves higher PSNR/SSIM on RealEstate10K interpolative, and DTU is incorrectly cited as [34] instead of [11].

Evaluation protocol has unclear aspects: target-view pose is required for projection/conditioning despite the 'pose-free' framing, and VGGT may have seen DTU during pretraining, potentially compromising the zero-shot claim.
Clarity and polish issues remain, including figure/table mismatches, grammar, and typographical errors such as learning rate '1×10' and 'weight W' instead of width.

strengths: Addresses a challenging and relevant problem: pose-free novel view synthesis with joint image and geometry synthesis, especially in extrapolative settings.
The proposed cross-modal attention instillation between image and geometry diffusion branches is a technically interesting and simple idea that could yield synergistic multi-task benefits.
Introduces proximity-based mesh conditioning with depth/normal cues to reduce erroneous projections from noisy or sparse point clouds.
Evaluates on multiple datasets and settings, including zero-shot DTU, in-domain RealEstate10K, Co3D, and qualitative comparisons against feedforward and warping-and-inpainting baselines.
Provides ablations for major components, robustness to synthetic geometry noise/sparsity, scaling to more reference views, and inference-time comparisons against large model-based NVS methods.
Reports practical efficiency metrics and plans to release code and weights, which supports reproducibility if fulfilled.
weaknesses: The method description is often unclear: exact architecture details of cross-modal attention instillation are missing, including how image-branch queries/keys are matched to geometry-branch layers, feature alignment, and training/inference schedules.

The central claim of aligned geometry synthesis lacks quantitative geometry comparisons against geometry prediction baselines such as DUSt3R, VGGT, Marigold, or NoPoSplat. Table 4 only varies the number of reference views rather than comparing against external geometry methods.

Comparison to large model-based NVS methods is partial and inconsistent: Table 7 reports only ViewCrafter and LVSM, while ZeroNVS and DUSt3R are shown qualitatively without quantitative evaluation or clear fairness controls.

Extrapolative evaluation relies heavily on pixel metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS), which may not adequately measure generative plausibility or hallucination quality. No FID, human study, or other generative metric is provided.

The pose-free / zero-shot claim may be compromised by reliance on VGGT for reference poses and geometry: if VGGT has seen the benchmark domains during pretraining, gains may not reflect true zero-shot generalization. No analysis of this overlap or VGGT failure cases is provided.

Proximity-based mesh conditioning is heuristic and insufficiently justified: ball-pivoting on noisy/dense point clouds can be unstable, and the normal-masking criterion is not ablated or theoretically motivated.
Ablation gains are relatively small (e.g., pointmap conditioning +0.38 PSNR, mesh conditioning +0.08 PSNR, cross-modal instillation +0.40 PSNR) and lack error bars or statistical significance tests.

The paper has clarity and copyediting issues: inconsistent 'instillation' vs. 'distillation' terminology, swapped or incorrect citations (e.g., VGGT/DUSt3R in the reference list), wrong DTU citation, and inconsistent dataset/table labels.

Reproducibility details are incomplete: dataset splits, exact evaluation protocol for extrapolative view selection, mesh hyperparameters, pointmap normalization details, and VGGT model version/configuration are not fully specified.

strengths: Addresses a relevant problem: joint pose-free novel view image and geometry synthesis, with a plausible warping-and-inpainting formulation.
The proposed cross-modal attention instillation uses image attention statistics to guide geometry completion, an interesting architectural direction for aligning modalities.
The multi-view aggregated attention and proximity-based mesh conditioning are intuitive and extend warping-inpainting to multi-view and noisy geometry settings.
The paper attempts qualitative and quantitative evaluation across Co3D, RealEstate10K, DTU, and several zero-shot datasets, and promises code/weights.
Ablation and robustness experiments (noise/sparsity) are provided, though limited to image metrics.
weaknesses: Evaluation protocol is flawed/inconsistent. The 'extrapolative' definition uses only camera position convex hull and ignores viewing direction; under this definition a 1-view target is always outside the convex hull, yet Table 1 reports 'interpolative' 1-view results. This undermines the central extrapolation claims.

Geometry evaluation is circular and insufficiently defined. Training uses pseudo ground-truth geometry from VGGT, and the Appendix states geometry MSE supervision uses VGGT predictions on target images; if evaluation compares to the same predictor, it does not measure true geometry. Standard 3D metrics (Chamfer distance, normal consistency) and geometry comparisons to baselines are largely absent.

Baselines are incomplete and possibly unfair. Main tables omit recent generative NVS methods (CAT3D, SV3D, ViewCrafter, LVSM, ZeroNVS) and some pose-free feedforward methods (DUSt3R/MASt3R), despite claiming state-of-the-art extrapolative NVS. Replacing baselines' geometry with VGGT may not reflect their original settings.

Method details are unclear or contradictory. It is not specified whether image Q/K are detached when used in the geometry branch, how image generation receives 'deterministic signals' from geometry completion, and whether training is joint or separate. The paper also inconsistently says 2-view training vs. 3 reference + 1 target view, and uses 'instillation' and 'distillation' interchangeably.

Key hyperparameters and reproducibility details are missing: ball-pivoting radius/thresholds, normal-masking rule, learning rate exponent, gradient accumulation, dataset splits, target geometry evaluation protocol, and mesh conversion runtime. Code is not yet available.

The central claims are stronger than the evidence. The ablation gains are small (baseline 16.55 to full 17.41 PSNR; MoAI adds 0.40 PSNR), no variance/confidence intervals are reported, and geometry quality is not ablated across components. 'High-fidelity' and 'state-of-the-art' are not supported by the reported numbers.
Geometry-related ablations and robustness analyses report only image metrics; they do not show that MoAI or proximity-based mesh conditioning improves aligned geometry, which is the core motivation.

The reference list is incomplete/corrupted, with a 'K.K.K.' filler line and missing citations for Zero123, ZeroNVS, CAT3D, MegaDepth, DepthAnything V3, etc. VGGT and DUSt3R references appear swapped, and Table 1 caption incorrectly cites DTU as Zhou et al. (2018). This is a serious scholarship/reproducibility issue.

Zero-shot DTU and in-domain RealEstate10K numbers are difficult to interpret: e.g., NoPoSplat's DTU numbers are far below its usual RealEstate10K performance, while Ours is only slightly better than baselines in some settings. The evaluation lacks clear camera overlap/visibility stratification.

strengths: Addresses a challenging setting: pose-free, sparse-view novel view synthesis with joint image and geometry generation, including extrapolative viewpoints.

Introduces cross-modal attention instillation (MoAI), a well-motivated mechanism that lets geometry and image diffusion branches share spatial attention maps; ablation and qualitative results support its synergistic benefit.
Proposes proximity-based mesh conditioning with depth/normal cues and normal masking, reducing erroneous projections from noisy off-the-shelf point clouds.
Provides strong empirical evidence: state-of-the-art extrapolative results on DTU and RealEstate10K, competitive interpolative performance, and qualitative comparisons on Co3D/Navi/in-the-wild data.
Evaluation is broad: zero-shot DTU, in-domain RealEstate10K, component ablations, robustness to Gaussian noise and sparsity, and scaling with number of reference views.

Computational efficiency is competitive: joint image+geometry inference in ~9.67s, with geometry branch reusing attention maps to save computation/memory; favorable against large model-based baselines.
Appendix adds useful details, qualitative ablations, robustness visualizations, and in-the-wild generalization results.
Clear relevance to novel view synthesis, 3D generation, and diffusion-based multi-task learning.
weaknesses: Relies heavily on an off-the-shelf geometry predictor (VGGT) for poses and pointmaps; end-to-end failure modes when that predictor degrades are not fully analyzed.

Geometry evaluation is limited: no comparison to specialized depth/completion baselines and no standard 3D metrics such as Chamfer distance or F-score; alignment claims remain largely qualitative or self-referential.
Ablation studies report mainly image metrics and not geometry metrics, so the quantitative contribution of components to geometric alignment is not fully established.

Reproducibility details are incomplete or contain typos (e.g., learning rate written as "1×10" without exponent; exact architecture, splits, training compute, and schedule details are partial); code/weights are promised but not yet released.

Baseline comparisons are somewhat inconsistent: DUSt3R is mentioned but not included in main tables, and large-model comparisons are mostly qualitative or relegated to the appendix without identical retraining conditions.
Minor writing/citation issues: "instillation" vs. "distillation" terminology is used inconsistently; DTU is cited as Zhou et al. (2018) in Table 1 rather than Jensen et al. (2014).

Novelty is moderate: the method combines existing warping-and-inpainting, geometry completion, attention sharing, and mesh conditioning, though the specific attention instillation is a useful addition.
No dedicated limitations section or broader ethical/societal discussion.
